description: Bean qou-slpd item 5. Settles whether the Newton-polygon slope is the q-Gevrey ORDER or the LEVEL — the last prose step in the C1 chain consumed by conj:qdifference-kernel-prolongation-symbol. RSZ section 1.3.2 makes order and level reciprocal, and the corpus had one 1/2 of each kind. The q-Euler equation, RSZ's own touchstone, has slope 1 where order and level coincide and therefore cannot decide the question. The family L_k = z^k sigma - 1 has Newton slope k, recursion c_m = q^{m-k} c_{m-k}, closed form c_{jk} = q^{k j (j-1)/2}, order 1/k and level k: the LEVEL tracks the slope, verified symbolically for k = 1, 2, 3 including the recursion at every index. Consequence for C1: its computed slope 1/2 read as a level predicts order 2 and growth q^{n^2}, which is the Lean-proved deg_q c_n = n^2; read as an order it would predict q^{n^2/4}, off by a factor 4 in the exponent and inconsistent with the corpus's own measurement.

computation.family: L_k = z^k*sigma - 1, sigma: z -> q z
computation.orderDefinition: lim 2 log_q |c_m| / m^2  (RSZ order s: a_n = O(A^n q^{s n^2/2}))

checks.name: recursion_from_operator_all_k
checks.detail: for k = [1, 2, 3], solving coeff(L_k f, z^m) = 0 returns c_m = q^(m-k) c_(m-k) for every m = k..14

checks.name: newton_slope_equals_qgevrey_level
checks.detail: for k = [1, 2, 3]: slope k, order 1/k, level k. slope == level in every case.

checks.name: q_euler_is_degenerate_higher_k_separates
checks.detail: at k=1 order and level coincide, so RSZ's own touchstone cannot distinguish them; at k>=2 they separate and level wins

checks.name: c1_growth_matches_slope_as_level
checks.detail: C1 slope 1/2 read as a LEVEL predicts order 2, growth q^{n^2}, which is the Lean-proved deg_q c_n = n^2. Read as an ORDER it would predict q^{n^2/4}, inconsistent with the corpus's own measured growth.

verdict: The Newton slope is the q-Gevrey LEVEL, not the order. Verified on the slope-k family for k = 1, 2, 3: slope k, order 1/k, level k. The k=1 case (q-Euler) is degenerate — order and level both equal 1 — which is why this went unexamined. For C1 the reading is forced rather than chosen: slope 1/2 as a level reproduces the Lean-proved q^{n^2} growth, as an order it would predict q^{n^2/4}. So theta_eq_half_gs_bridge's grounding of c1Slope = 1/2 through routeB_gaussian_order_half uses the wrong quantity of the wrong sequence; the right grounding is the inf-side LEVEL, which is c1InfCoeff_order_two restated. The NUMBER 1/2 was never in doubt and no downstream conclusion changes — Door-i needs only that the two slope multisets differ, which is now newtonSlopes_c1_ne_ggm.
